rfi.title: Israel's recognition of the Armenian genocide unsettles Turkey and Azerbaijan
rfi.description: Israel's parliament voted on 29 June 2026 to recognise the 1915 Armenian genocide, breaking with decades of official reticence on the issue. RFI spoke to three regional experts to unpack the politics behind the vote and its fallout: Gerald Steinberg, professor at Bar-Ilan University in Tel Aviv; Richard Giragossian, director of the Regional Studies Centre in Yerevan; and Ilter Turan, professor at Bilgi University in Istanbul.

rfi.title: Bayeux Tapestry delivered to British Museum under cover of darkness

rfi.title: Fifteen years of independence for South Sudan, but still little to celebrate
rfi.description: South Sudan, the world's youngest country, on Thursday marks the 15th anniversary of its independence, following decades of war with Sudan, a 2005 peace agreement and a 2011 self-determination referendum in which almost 99 percent of voters backed statehood. But the hopes that came with it have given way to renewed conflict, economic collapse and political deadlock.

rfi.title: Secrecy surrounds Bayeux Tapestry's imminent Channel crossing
rfi.description: Under cover of darkness and heavy police guard, the Bayeux Tapestry – a 68-metre embroidered chronicle of the Norman conquest of England, stitched in wool not long after the events it depicts – is set to cross the Channel within days, the official overseeing its move to London has revealed.

rfi.title: How appeal court verdict against Le Pen puts her back in the running for 2027
rfi.description: A French appeals court this week upheld Marine Le Pen's conviction for embezzling funds from the European Parliament and sentenced her to house arrest – something the far-right leader previously said would rule her out of France's 2027 presidential race. Yet Le Pen still has one last legal recourse to overturn her conviction and, pending that appeal, remains free to hit the campaign trail.

rfi.title: Trump says US will give Ukraine licence to build Patriot missiles

lemonde.description: Le bon bilan de la France en matière de baisse des émissions de gaz à effet de serre repose en partie sur une illusion comptable : la désindustrialisation l’oblige à importer massivement des biens fortement carbonés, comme le constate une note de Rexecode, que présente Béatrice Madeline dans sa chronique.

france24fr.title: Périscolaire à Paris : un ex-animateur condamné pour agressions sexuelles, une première
france24fr.description: La justice a condamné vendredi un ancien animateur à 18 mois de prison avec sursis pour des agressions sexuelles commises sur une enfant dans un centre de loisirs parisien, entre octobre 2023 et juillet 2025. Le tribunal s'est appuyé sur la "cohérence" et la "crédibilité particulière" de la parole de la victime, aujourd'hui âgée de six ans.

france24fr.title: À la frontière irakienne, l'Iran multiplie les attaques contre les groupes dissidents kurdes
france24fr.description: Les forces militaires iraniennes ont récemment mené des frappes aériennes massives contre les bases militaires de milices kurdes iraniennes, situées au Kurdistan irakien (nord - ouest). Ces attaques, sans précédent, témoignent de la crainte de Téhéran de voir ces milices devenir plus offensives à la faveur de l’instabilité générée par la guerre avec Israël et les Etats-Unis.

france24fr.title: Antonio Tajani : "Nous ne sommes pas contre les immigrés, nous voulons la migration régulière"
france24fr.description: Cette semaine, Caroline de Camaret reçoit Antonio Tajani, ministre italien des Affaires étrangères et vice-président du gouvernement de Giorgia Meloni – une coalition tripartite allant de son parti, Forza Italia, à la droite radicale (Frères d'Italie, La Ligue). Il fait un tour d'horizon de l'actualité internationale vue de l'Italie meloniste et revient sur les réformes migratoires et institutionnelles controversées.

france24fr.title: Taïwan : les traditionnelles cueilleuses d’algues rouges risquent de disparaître
france24fr.description: À 72 ans, Wu Feng-chiao, l'une des dernières personnes de Taïwan à cueillir des algues pour les transformer en gelée, reste imperturbable face aux vagues qui déferlent sur elle. Lorsque cette génération de "hainu", ou "femmes de la mer", ne sera plus en mesure de continuer, cette activité risque de disparaître. Les jeunes Taïwanais préfèrent vivre en ville plutôt que dans le nord-est reculé de l'île.

france24fr.title: Droits des passagers aériens renforcés : le ciel européen s'éclaircit
france24fr.description: Malgré les émissions de CO2, l'avion a toujours la cote : un milliard de passagers par an volent dans le ciel européen, et l'Union européenne (UE) défend les droits de ces passagers face aux compagnies aériennes. Un accord a été trouvé le 15 juin au sein de l'Union pour réformer le règlement européen sur les droits des passagers aériens, après treize ans de négociation.

france24fr.title: Tour de France : le Belge Tim Merlier s'impose au sprint lors de la 7e étape
france24fr.description: Le Belge Tim Merlier a remporté vendredi la septième étape du Tour de France à Bordeaux, au terme d'un sprint massif. Il a devancé le Norvégien Soren Waerenskjold et l'Érythréen Biniam Girmay. À 33 ans, le coureur décroche sa quatrième victoire sur la Grande Boucle, après celles de Pontivy (2021), Dunkerque et Châteauroux (2025).

france24fr.title: En Mauritanie, le paradis menacé de la pêche traditionnelle des Imraguen
france24fr.description: C'est un mode de vie multiséculaire qui se transmet de génération en génération. Mais le réchauffement climatique risque d'y mettre fin. On vous propose de passer quelques minutes avec les Imraguen, un peuple de pêcheurs du désert mauritanien, à la jonction entre le Sahara aride et l'océan Atlantique. Récit de Ludovic de Foucaud.

france24fr.title: Crimes de guerre au Soudan : l'ONU enquête dans les camps de réfugiés du Tchad
france24fr.description: La guerre au Soudan impacte directement ses voisins, comme le Tchad, où les Nations Unies ont intensifié le rythme de leurs visites ces derniers mois. L'objectif : trouver une issue à ce conflit. L'envoyé spécial du secrétaire général de l'ONU s'est rendu dans les camps de réfugiés de l'est du pays, tandis que la procureure adjointe de la Cour Pénale Internationale était à N'Djamena. Précisions d’Harold Girard, correspondant de France 24.

france24fr.title: Soudan : Rencontre avec une habitante d'El-Obeid, où l'ONU craint un bain de sang
france24fr.description: La capitale de l'État du Kordofan du Nord au Soudan, El-Obeid, est encerclée par les Forces de Soutien Rapide. L'ONU dit craindre un bain de sang. La population est exsangue. Environ 600 000 civils y résideraient toujours. Notre correspondant régional, Bastien Renouil, a pu contacter l'un d'eux.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : l'opposition rentre du Burundi après des consultations pour sortir le pay de la crise
france24fr.description: Ils sont de retour à Kinshasa après leur visite à Bujumbura dans un contexte de vive tension autour de la révision de la Constitution. Les opposants congolais ont présenté les conclusions des consultations avec le président burundais, Évariste Ndayishimiye, président en exercice de l’Union africaine. À cette occasion, ils ont une nouvelle fois plaidé en faveur d'un dialogue politique inclusif pour tenter de sortir le pays de la crise politique. Précisions d’Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula, corresponda

france24fr.title: Les Antilles envahies par les sargasses, situation critique dans onze communes martiniquaises
france24fr.description: Aux Antilles, des plages sont transformées en tapis d'algues. En se décomposant, les gaz toxiques libérés par les algues sargasses dépassent le seuil de tolérance, rendant l'air irrespirable. En Martinique, la situation est critique dans onze communes. Un centre d'accueil a ouvert ses portes pour les riverains les plus exposés.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les Égyptiens accueillis en héros à leur retour au pays
france24fr.description: La sélection égyptienne de football a reçu un accueil triomphal vendredi à son retour au pays, où des milliers de supporters sont venus saluer son parcours historique à la Coupe du monde, achevé en huitième de finale face à l'Argentine.

france24fr.title: L'équipe égyptienne de football entourés des supporters à leur retour
france24fr.description: Des milliers de supporters égyptiens se sont rassemblés vendredi pour accueillir l’équipe nationale de football à son retour au pays. Les Pharaons, qui ont pour la première fois de leur histoire atteint les huitièmes de finale du tournoi, ont quitté l'Amérique du Nord après leur défaite 3-2 face à l’Argentine. Récit d’Étienne Paponaud.

france24fr.title: Erling Haaland : le footballeur norvégien de tous les records
france24fr.description: Il aide la #Norvège à performer au #Mondial2026 et il est considéré comme l’un des meilleurs buteurs au monde. Il s’agit de Erling Haaland. Le “cyborg” norvégien bat tous les records. Mais permettra-t-il une nouvelle victoire en quarts de finale face à l’#Angleterre ?

france24fr.title: Soudan : le difficile quotidien des habitants d'El-Obeid, encerclée par les FSR
france24fr.description: Au Soudan, l’ONU redoute un bain de sang à El-Obeid, encerclée par les Forces de soutien rapide. Environ 600 000 civils y seraient toujours piégés dans une ville à bout de souffle. Témoignage rare d’un habitant.

france24fr.title: Taïwan se prépare à l'arrivée du typhon "Bavi"
france24fr.description: Le typhon Bavi poursuit son chemin destructeur. Après avoir déjà frappé plusieurs îles du Pacifique et fait quinze morts aux Philippines, il doit toucher le nord et l'est de Taïwan vendredi et samedi, ainsi que les îles du sud du Japon, avant de s'abattre sur la Chine. Récit d’Anna Pereira.

france24fr.title: La France se prépare avec la 4e brigade d’aérocombat aux missions aériennes
france24fr.description:
Dans notre mini-série ‘La France se prépare’, embarquez avec la 4ᵉ brigade d'aérocombat pour un exercice aérien à Chaumont.  
 
Nos reporters Elisabeth Allain et Geoges Yazbeck se sont retrouvés à bord d'un NH90 Caïman, immersion au cœur d'une mission aérienne simulant l'attaque d'une cible au sol.

france24fr.title: Des entrepreneurs fortunés achètent des forêts pour ne rien en faire
france24fr.description: Ils sont millionnaires, écolos et achètent des forêts…pour surtout ne rien en faire. C'est une démarche qui gagne en popularité chez les entrepreneurs à succès : sanctuariser des domaines entiers pour protéger la biodiversité. C'est le cas du domaine du Costil, 170 hectares de forêt normande laissés en libre évolution, devenu un refuge pour des centaines d’espèces animales et végétales. C'est aussi un lieu de partage à travers les évènements de sensibilisation à la protection du vivant.

spiegel.title: Geopolitik: »China hat Russland genau dort, wo es Russland haben möchte«
spiegel.description: Xi und Putin eint mehr als Geopolitik: Beide haben sich beim anderen abgeschaut, wie man Macht auf eine Person zuschneidet. Der Politikwissenschaftler Björn Alexander Düben über eine Verbindung, die enger ist, als sie scheint.

spiegel.title: Anschlag auf Geschäftsmann: Eine blutige Spur führt von Monaco bis nach Kyjiw
spiegel.description: Die Hauptverdächtige des Bombenattentats in Monaco ist offenbar tot. Die Männer, die sie beauftragt und umgebracht haben sollen, kommen von ukrainischen Geheimdiensten. Der Kriminalfall bringt Kyjiw in Erklärungsnot.

spiegel.title: In Mali jagen die Rebellen wieder russische Söldner
spiegel.description: Aufständische Tuareg und Dschihadisten haben russische Söldner aus dem sogenannten Afrika-Korps angegriffen. Außenminister Sergej Lawrow umwirbt derweil die Mächtigen in Portugals Ex-Kolonie Mosambik.

spiegel.title: China - wiederverwendbare Rakete »Langer Marsch 10B«: Volksrepublik fängt erstmals Stufe auf
spiegel.description: China schließt zu den USA auf – als zweites Land auf der Welt verfügt die Volksrepublik nun über eine zuverlässige Technik für wiederverwendbare Raketen. Damit erfüllen die Entwickler den gerade angelaufenen neuen Fünfjahresplan.

spiegel.title: Frank-Walter Steinmeier zieht um: Sehnsucht nach Schloss Bellevue bleibt
spiegel.description: Am Freitagmorgen hat Bundespräsident Frank-Walter Steinmeier die Türen zu seinem neuen Amts- und Arbeitszimmer geöffnet. In der Luft lag die Sehnsucht nach Schloss Bellevue, aus dem er ausziehen musste.

spiegel.title: Trump wollte 20.000 Soldaten für seine Friedenstruppe in Gaza. Es werden jetzt wohl erst mal zehn bis 20
spiegel.description: Ein Vorauskommando aus Marokko hätte eigentlich im Juni im Gazastreifen ankommen sollen. Doch bislang ist kein einziger Soldat der sogenannten Internationalen Stabilisierungsgruppe in der Palästinenserenklave aufgetaucht.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Norwegen gehen vor Viertelfinale offenbar Großbilschirme für Public Viewing aus
spiegel.description: Die WM-Euphorie in Norwegen bringt viele Gemeinden an ihre Public-Viewing-Grenzen. Ex-Weltmeister Xavi prophezeit Lamine Yamal eine große Zukunft. Und: Der Shootingstar der Schweiz fällt gegen Argentinien aus. Die WM-News.

spiegel.title: Japan: Ehe eine Frau den Thron besteigt, wird der Tennō adoptiert
spiegel.description: Das japanische Kaiserpaar hat eine Tochter, doch eine weibliche Thronfolgerin hält man in dem Land offenbar für den worst case. Das Unterhaus in Tokio hat stattdessen für Plan B votiert.

spiegel.title: Wimbledon 2026: Alexander Zverev zu stark für Arthur Fery
spiegel.description: Zum ersten Mal seit 1995 steht mit Alexander Zverev wieder ein deutscher Spieler im Männerfinale von Wimbledon. Der Liebling des Publikums Arthur Fery war machtlos gegen den selbstbewussten Aufschlagriesen.

spiegel.title: Ungarn erhält von der EU zehn Milliarden Euro
spiegel.description: Unter Viktor Orbán war das Geld noch eingefroren, nun erhält Budapest üppige Mittel aus dem EU-Wiederaufbaufonds. Zugleich vollzog Ungarn einen wichtigen Schritt zur Korruptionsbekämpfung.

spiegel.title: Iran: Machthaber Mojtaba Khamenei ist nicht bei der Trauerfeier für seinen Vater aufgetaucht
spiegel.description: Selbst bei der pompösen Bestattungszeremonie für seinen Vater und Vorgänger Ali Khamenei fehlte Irans Revolutionsführer Mojtaba. Gerüchte wuchern. Aber was bedeutet seine Abwesenheit wirklich?

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: US-Präsident wirbt für Billigtankstellen »Freedom Fuels«
spiegel.description: Die Benzinpreise in den USA sind seit Donald Trumps Irankrieg enorm gestiegen. Nun greift der US-Präsident zu einer ungewöhnlichen PR-Maßnahme.

spiegel.title: E-Autos: Förderung befeuert Markt – ausländische Hersteller profitieren
spiegel.description: Die Beratungsfirma EY sieht in der staatlichen E-Auto-Prämie einen »massiven Booster«. Konzernen aus China und den USA kommt sie aber stärker zugute als jenen aus Deutschland.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Kai Wegner gibt auf, Heizungsgesetz gekippt, Jimi Blue Ochsenknecht wieder vor Gericht
spiegel.description: Berlins Regierender Tennisspieler gibt die Spitzenkandidatur als Bürgermeister auf. Die Bundesregierung beerdigt Habecks »Heizhammer«. Und Jimi Blue Ochsenknecht muss erneut vor Gericht. Das ist die Lage am Freitagabend.

spiegel.title: Kommentar: Kai Wegner: Rückzug des Bürgermeisters kommt für Berlin zu spät
spiegel.description: Kai Wegner hätte als Reformer der chaotischen Berliner Verwaltung in die Stadtgeschichte eingehen können. Stattdessen wurde er zur Witzfigur mit Tennisschläger.

spiegel.title: Tour de France: Tim Merlier sprintet zum Sieg – deutscher Tour-Debütant Max Kanter Vierter
spiegel.description: Seit Nils Politt 2022 hat kein Deutscher mehr eine Etappe bei der wichtigsten Rundfahrt des Weltradsports gewonnen. Auch Tour-Neuling Max Kanter musste sich im Sprint geschlagen geben.

spiegel.title: Kelela, neues Album »New Avatar«: Selbst die Gitarren ergeben sich ihr seufzend
spiegel.description: Jazz, Soul, Dance und jetzt auch noch Rock: Auf ihrem vierten Album »New Avatar« integriert die US-Sängerin Kelela die Gitarrenmusik ihrer Jugend in ihren fließenden Sound. Und: die besten Songs der Woche.

spiegel.title: Ryanair-Flug von Thessaloniki nach Memmingen: Maschine war schon am Donnerstag einmal umgekehrt
spiegel.description: Bei einem Flug Richtung Memmingen wurde ein Passagier fast aus einer Boeing 737 NG gezogen, als ein Fenster zerbrach. Was bisher bekannt ist und welchen Rat das Luftfahrt-Bundesamt Passagieren gibt.

observador.title: "O Candidato Perfeito": a nova ficção da Rádio Observador
observador.description: Estreou a sequela de "Zé faz 25", focada num empresário candidato à autarquia de Lisboa que enfrenta o desaparecimento do filho. A série combina mistério policial com intriga política.

observador.title: As notícias das 18h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Jesus e os cinco mandamentos da primeira aula de 45 minutos
observador.description: Emocionou-se pelo orgulho em ser português, soltou-se nas perguntas, fez rir, refletiu sobre médios num 4x3x3 e falou do Mundial sem falar – dizendo que a sua ideia não tem nada a ver com a anterior.

observador.title: Acidente com cinco viaturas corta sentido norte-sul na Ponte
observador.description: O acidente envolveu cinco veículos e ocorreu pelas 17h00, causando seis feridos. As autoridades mobilizaram 25 operacionais para o local.

observador.title: Chuva de lama num fim de semana com trovoadas e raios
observador.description: Vai chover no litoral, incluindo em Lisboa e Porto. E haverá trovoadas, cujo perigo muitos desconhecem: 24 mil pessoas morrem por ano devido aos raios. E também chegam poeiras, com chuva de lama.

observador.title: Ateou fogo a rulote onde julgava estar o companheiro
observador.description: O fogo foi ateado em contexto de violência doméstica, agravado pelo consumo de bebidas alcoólicas. O veículo ficou totalmente destruído após as chamas se propagarem por toda a sua estrutura.

observador.title: Maior central solar encravada há dois anos na justiça
observador.description: Desde 2024 que a autorização ambiental dada à central solar Fernando Pessoa foi suspensa por decisão do juiz e após impugnação do Ministério Público. Agência do Ambiente recorreu, mas não há decisão.

observador.title: Grândola. Queda de parapente faz ferido grave
observador.description: A vítima é um homem luxemburguês de 65 anos. Após o incidente, foi transportado em estado grave num helicóptero do Instituto Nacional de Emergência Médica para o Hospital do Litoral Alentejano.

observador.title: Música com IA passa a ter rótulo nos serviços de streaming
observador.description: IFPI, Grammy, SAG-AFTRA e RIAA unem-se para identificar canções como "Criada por IA" ou "Com a ajuda de IA". No Deezer, 44% das músicas já são geradas por IA.

observador.title: JSD leva jovens a Bruxelas para conhecerem projeto europeu
observador.description: O Fórum da Autonomia, promovido pela JSD e pelo eurodeputado Paulo Cabral, realiza-se entre quarta e sexta-feira e inclui visitas ao PE, à Comissão Europeia e à NATO.

observador.title: México suspeita do FBI na captura de chefes do cartel
observador.description: Fundador do cartel de Sinaloa e filho de "El Chapo" foram detidos há dois em anos em El Paso, no Texas. Washington continua a negar qualquer envolvimento, mas suspeitas do México continuam a existir.

observador.title: 17h. EUA prontos para regressar à mesa de negociações
observador.description: Donald Trump diz que concordou com pedido iraniano para retomar processo negocial, mas deixa aviso: o cessar fogo acabou. Ainda, Rui Tavares garante que Livre está preparado para funções governativas.

observador.title: Irão. "Provavelmente evitou-se aqui uma escalada maior"
observador.description: Bruno Cardoso Reis vê com bons olhos o regresso às negociações entre EUA e Irão. Ainda assim, o historiador alerta para o facto das decisões de Donald Trump serem muitas vezes pouco duradouras.

observador.title: Instrutor saltou de avião. Aluna de 22 anos aterrou sozinha
observador.description: Leandro Bertazzo, 42 anos, saltou pela porta do Cessna C-150 a 250 metros de altitude em Córdoba, na Argentina. Dias antes tinha tido uma consulta numa clínica psiquiátrica.

observador.title: Trump. Negociações com Irão continuam mas cessar-fogo acabou
observador.description: EUA e Irão retomam negociações, mas Trump garante que tréguas estão encerradas. Na quarta-feira, Washington atacou cerca de 90 instalações militares iranianas.

observador.title: Privadas denunciam exclusão de fundos na Provedoria
observador.description: O programa Centro 2030 reserva fundos europeus para residências apenas a instituições públicas. APESP diz que estudantes carenciados do privado ficam prejudicados.

observador.title: PCP diz que audição a 21 de julho é "inconcebível"
observador.description: Paulo Raimundo diz ser "completamente inconcebível" que Fernando Alexandre só se disponha a ser ouvido após as férias. Chega também pressiona e propõe dia 17 de julho.

observador.title: Idosos. Número de vítimas de crime aumenta 30,5% em 6 anos
observador.description: Foram registadas 288.632 vítimas, entre as quais 44.161 idosos em 2025. A maioria dos crimes de que os idosos são vítimas é contra o património, seguidos de ilícitos contra as pessoas.

elpais.title: Últimas noticias del incendio forestal de Los Gallardos (Almería), en directo | El incendio de Almería se cobra 12 vidas y obliga a evacuar a un millar de personas
elpais.description: Marlaska afirma que hasta el momento se han formalizado tres denuncias por desapariciones, aunque hay 23 personas que continúan sin ser localizadas | Ocho heridos, cuatro de ellos graves | Las primeras investigaciones apuntan a la caída de un cable eléctrico

elpais.title: Viento, barrancos y decenas de casas diseminadas: la noche infernal de Bédar
elpais.description: El alcalde de la localidad donde han fallecido 12 personas, Francisco Collado, alertó del peligro a sus vecinos puerta a puerta, con megáfonos de la Policía Local y hasta con las campanas de la iglesia

elpais.title: Así son las imágenes aéreas del incendio de Los Gallardos (Almería)
elpais.description: Los vídeos difundidos por la Guardia Civil muestran el avance del fuego en el municipio almeriense

elpais.title: Una mujer rescatada en el incendio de Los Gallardos: “Nos dieron diez minutos para coger lo esencial”
elpais.description: “No sabemos cómo estará nuestra casa: ojalá los bomberos la hayan salvado”, lamentan otro superviviente

elpais.title: Los tres elementos que funcionan como un acelerador del fuego
elpais.description: El viento, el calor y el escaso cuidado del terreno aceleran la propagación de los incendios en un escenario de cambio climático cada vez más evidente

elpais.title: “Es importante confinarse y nunca autoevacuarse”, la advertencia de los bomberos ante la tragedia de Almería
elpais.description: La Generalitat asegura que las actuaciones realizadas en puntos estratégicos permiten limitar incendios forestales en Cataluña

elpais.title: ¿Dónde se han producido las muertes? Mapas del fatal incendio en Almería
elpais.description: El fuego se propagó a gran velocidad sobre una zona escarpada, de casas aisladas y caminos de tierra donde las víctimas quedaron atrapadas

elpais.title: Qué hacer y qué no en caso de ser sorprendido por un incendio forestal como el de Los Gallardos
elpais.description: Si las autoridades decretan una evacuación, es prioritario seguir la orden y por las rutas indicadas. No se deben tomar atajos por caminos forestales

elpais.title: El incendio de Almería y el fin de la excepcionalidad
elpais.description: Cada verano nos sorprendemos con los grandes incendios que asolan el país como si fueran una anomalía. Pero ya son la norma, y hace falta un pacto de Estado para atajarlos

elpais.title: La Guardia Civil investiga la caída de un cable eléctrico como desencadenante del incendio en Los Gallardos
elpais.description: Endesa asegura que el tendido no es de su red, no tenía tensión y estaba abandonado desde hacía años. Red Eléctrica también afirma que la infraestructura no le pertenece

elpais.title: El incendio de Los Gallardos en Almería, en imágenes
elpais.description: Unas 1.000 personas han sido desalojadas de forma preventiva. Algunas de las víctimas han sido localizadas sin vida en el interior de vehículos que habían sido alcanzados por las llamas, en una pedanía del municipio vecino de Bédar, según ha informado el 112 de Andalucía en un comunicado

elpais.title: Cronología del incendio de Los Gallardos, el más mortal del siglo en España
elpais.description: El incendio forestal desatado este jueves en el municipio de Almería sigue activo 24 horas después, tras dejar 12 muertos, unas 3.200 hectáreas arrasadas y cientos de vecinos desalojados por el rápido avance del viento

elpais.title: España - Bélgica en directo | Fabián entra por Pedri en el once de la selección
elpais.description: La selección busca meterse en una semifinal de la Copa del Mundo por segunda vez en su historia |Francia será el rival de La Roja si los de De la Fuente superan esta noche a los belgas

elpais.title: Cucurella: “Soy muy intenso, trabajo para que el rival nunca se sienta cómodo”
elpais.description: El lateral habla de la Roja y de cómo le convenció Mourinho para fichar por el Real Madrid

elpais.title: Mundial 2026: Programa ‘Fútbol chapa’ | España y Bélgica, previa jugador por jugador
elpais.description: El análisis del duelo de La Roja por un puesto en semifinales, con Diego Torres y Ramon Besa

elpais.title: Luis de la Fuente: “El mejor Lamine está por llegar; ahora es muy peligroso para los rivales”
elpais.description: El seleccionador, muy relajado antes del partido de cuartos de España contra Bélgica, cree que el azulgrana necesita recuperar su “brillantez” tras la lesión

elpais.title: Más allá del debut de Borja Iglesias
elpais.description: Vivimos en un momento en el que lo fácil es no pronunciarse sobre nada y esperar a que pase la tormenta, sin embargo, el Panda eligió otro camino

elpais.title: Marruecos piensa ya en el Mundial 2030 tras quedar eliminado ante Francia
elpais.description: Los Leones del Atlas asumen desde la élite del fútbol la derrota ante la selección gala para encarar la próxima Copa del Mundo como aspirante a ganarla

nyt.title: Two Days of U.S. Strikes in Iran Signal a Sharp Escalation
nyt.description: U.S. forces hit more than 170 targets, including air defense systems, drone and missile storage sites, and military speedboats.

nyt.title: The U.S. and Iran Are Fighting Again. Is the Cease-Fire Over?
nyt.description: Eric Schmitt, a New York Times National Security correspondent, analyzes recent skirmishes between the U.S. and Iran and whether they threaten ongoing negotiations for a peace deal.

nyt.title: Iran’s Supreme Leader Remains Absent, a Void at the Top of the Regime
nyt.description: Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei did not appear at his father’s funeral this week, fueling speculation about his physical condition and leaving a power vacuum in a divided country.

nyt.title: Mediators Trying to Pull U.S. and Iran Back From Brink, Officials Say
nyt.description: Qatari mediators were in Iran seeking to salvage the tattered truce. President Trump said talks with Tehran would continue, even if the cease-fire was “over.”

nyt.title: New Air Force One Lacks Defensive Countermeasures of Previous Model, Officials Say
nyt.description: Experts said the lack of such capabilities poses a potential risk when the president travels overseas. The White House defended the aircraft’s safety.

nyt.title: Trump Administration Fires Members of Independent Election Group
nyt.description: The firings and a resignation render the Election Assistance Commission useless. The moves come as President Trump seeks to impose control over how ballots will be counted in the midterms.

nyt.title: Witnesses of ICE Killing in Houston Dispute the Official Account
nyt.description: The agency said a Mexican immigrant driving a van tried to ram agents before they shot him dead. A lawyer for three passengers said that was untrue.

nyt.title: At Least 21 People Have Been Shot by Federal Immigration Agents Since Last Year
nyt.description: Many of them have been shot in their cars. Five have died, including three U.S. citizens. Here are their names and what we know about the circumstances.

nyt.title: Why Some Women in Maine Are Mourning the End of Graham Platner’s Campaign
nyt.description: They believe the accuser, but they also grieve the demise of a campaign that promised that politics could be different — and they blame those who failed to find a less flawed candidate.

nyt.title: Eight Years Later, They’re Still Restoring a House Bought at Auction
nyt.description: First-time buyers from the Bay Area won an abandoned house at a Kingston, N.Y., tax auction. Eight years later, they’re still restoring it.

nyt.title: An Aging Assassin Was Caught by ICE. Will the U.S. Deport Him?
nyt.description: He helped plot a car bombing in Washington that killed two people in 1976. Fifty years later, old government secrets could decide his fate.

nyt.title: The Work of Helping A.I. Destroy Work
nyt.description: Start-ups are paying white-collar professionals to teach their jobs to artificial intelligence models. It’s a bonanza. It’s bleak. Where will it end?

nyt.title: How Terrorist Groups Are Using A.I. to Gain an Edge in Battle
nyt.description: A.I. chatbots are not just a propaganda tool for violent extremists but are aiding in bomb construction and attack planning, new research finds.

nyt.title: A.I. Has Rewarded Investors. It May Now Pose Their Greatest Risk.
nyt.description: Near the midpoint of the year, stocks and bonds both report good returns. But the global stock market has become highly concentrated, our columnist says.

nyt.title: Trump Is Promoting ‘Freedom Fuel’ for $3.47 a Gallon. Who’s Behind It?
nyt.description: The president has praised a network of 25 recently rebranded gas stations in the Philadelphia region that have been selling gas for considerably less than the national average.

nyt.title: China Launches Reusable Rocket, Clearing a Key Hurdle in Race With SpaceX
nyt.description: The launch and recovery of the Long March 10B could represent a long-awaited breakthrough for Chinese satellite companies.

nyt.title: How Volkswagen’s Troubles Were Made in China
nyt.description: The German auto giant’s push into China powered it for decades, but now the company faces fierce competition from Chinese automakers in markets around the world.

nyt.title: This Star Just Ate a Planet, and It’s Not Done Yet
nyt.description: A star 1,300 light-years away appears to have just consumed one world and is gearing up for seconds.

npr.title: U.S.-Iran fighting appears to pause. And, life inside Israel's military zones in Gaza
npr.description: Fighting between the U.S. and Iran appears to have paused after two days of clashing amid a shaky ceasefire. And, a look at what life is like inside Israel's expanding zone of control in Gaza.

npr.title: Count Binface: The intergalactic warrior who could upend Britain's strangest election
npr.description: Meet Count Binface: the challenger from another planet taking on Nigel Farage as questions over the Reform UK leader's finances overshadow his election comeback.

npr.title: 9 months into a ceasefire, Israel now controls nearly 70% of Gaza
npr.description: When the U.S. brokered a ceasefire last year, Israel controlled half of Gaza. Now Israeli forces have pushed deeper, and Palestinians are paying a deadly price.

npr.title: One of Spain's deadliest wildfires kills at least 12 people, with 23 others missing
npr.description: Several victims of the fire in the southern province of Almeria, a popular holiday destination, were found inside burnt-out vehicles and were thought to have died while trying to flee the flames.

npr.title: Ebola death toll reaches 600, as new cases suspected in other parts of Congo
npr.description: New suspected cases of Ebola have been reported in parts of Congo that were previously unaffected, the government said, signaling the continued spread of the disease beyond the epicenter in Ituri.

npr.title: U.S. and Iran exchange intensifying fire across Mideast, threatening ceasefire deal
npr.description: Back-and-forth attacks have repeatedly threatened the ceasefire, but Thursday's appeared bigger all around.

npr.title: Former U.S. envoy reacts to Iran strikes and NATO summit
npr.description: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with former U.S. Ambassador to NATO Nicholas Burns regarding this week's developments in the U.S.-Iran conflict -- and the NATO summit this week.

npr.title: Where are Iran and Ukraine wars headed after NATO summit?
npr.description: Fresh strikes between Iran and the United States and a tense ceasefire scrapped — Is the war with Iran back on?

npr.title: Graham Platner ends Senate bid. And, why Nolan Wells' death captured national attention
npr.description: Democrat Graham Platner ended his bid last night for U.S. Senate. And, prominent civil rights attorney Ben Crump has been enlisted to help get answers in the July Fourth weekend death of Nolan Wells.

npr.title: How England's class divide shaped Andy Burnham, the U.K.'s likely next prime minister
npr.description: As mayor of Manchester, Andy Burnham brought growth to the postindustrial city. Can he scale that nationally as the next prime minister?

lanacion.title: Confirmado por Hochul: la nueva sede central de American Express llega a Manhattan y creará 3200 nuevos empleos
lanacion.description: American Express tendrá una nueva sede global en Manhattan, una torre de 55 pisos que generará miles de empleos durante su construcción hasta 2031.

lanacion.description: Los patentamientos superan con creces al 2025, pero hay un sector que muestra un impulso que podría consolidarse al alza en el mediano plazo

lanacion.description: Se desempeñaba como consejero titular de Minería de la provincia; la lista de casos similares en esa región

lanacion.description: En un móvil de LN+, el cocinero compartió los secretos de la receta, explicó por qué el caldo debe comenzar con agua fría, qué corte de carne recomienda y cuál es el ingrediente que, según él, nunca debería llevar el plato

lanacion.description: Ocurrió en un colegio de Flores; el alumno cerró el discurso con un mensaje de apoyo al equipo dirigido por Lionel Scaloni; el video se volvió viral y fue celebrado por la propia institución

lanacion.description: El encuentro de cuartos de final se disputará este sábado a las 18 (hora argentina) en el estadio de Miami con arbitraje de Clément Turpin

lanacion.description: El índice elaborado por el JP Morgan se ubica en 403 puntos básicos; la última vez que estuvo debajo de los 400 puntos fue en abril de 2018

lanacion.description: La reacción de la prensa de Francia luego de la victoria por 2 a 0 ante Marruecos. Los galos esperan en las semifinales por el ganador de España y Bélgica que juegan hoy a las 16 de Argentina

lanacion.description: El minuto a minuto de las últimas noticias de la selección argentina, declaraciones de los jugadores y entrenadores, y repercusiones sobre los partidos

phys-org.title: Math reveals how honeybee hives balance the 'daring few, patient many' strategy
phys-org.description: How do bees make group decisions without a leader? Math experts have determined that the best strategy is for a few to assume the risk of foraging under all conditions while the majority stay safely back and forage only when conditions are favorable.

phys-org.title: Tropical forests can switch from carbon sinks to carbon sources during El Niño
phys-org.description: Tropical forests draw down and store large quantities of CO₂ from the atmosphere. The Amazon rainforest in South America, for example, stores approximately 123 billion tons of carbon—more than is stored in any other terrestrial ecosystem in the world. But these forests are facing a critical challenge.

phys-org.title: Research identifies farming practices that improve irrigation efficiency
phys-org.description: Mississippi State scientists are building on two decades of irrigation research to identify production practices that help growers save water while improving crop yields.

phys-org.title: New test certifies quantum measurements that simpler methods cannot mimic
phys-org.description: Proving that one quantum measurement is more powerful than another has long been difficult. Physicists from Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf, Lund University and the University of Innsbruck have now developed and demonstrated a simple technique to certify that a certain class of measurements has properties that cannot be mimicked by simpler means. Their paper is published in the journal PRX Quantum.

phys-org.title: Artificial hand reproduces human gestures using memory written into light-responsive polymers
phys-org.description: Danqing Liu from Eindhoven University of Technology explores how interactions with digital systems can be improved through the sense of touch. To achieve this, she develops advanced liquid crystal polymers that respond to light. Her work has recently been published in two scientific journals, Science Advances and Matter & Light.

phys-org.description: A large cemetery containing the lavishly adorned remains of unidentified high-status individuals dating from around 2,000 years ago has been uncovered by archaeologists from Archaeology South-East (UCL Institute of Archaeology). phys-org.title: Report shows declining gun homicides, record gun suicides in 2024
phys-org.description: Nearly 45,000 people in the U.S. died by gun violence in 2024—one person every 12 minutes, on average—and an all-time high of 27,593 died by firearm suicide, according to the latest annual firearm mortality report from the Johns Hopkins Center for Gun Violence Solutions at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.

phys-org.title: Researchers discover genetic secrets of mung bean crops
phys-org.description: Researchers at the Center for Crop and Food Innovation (CCFI) have made a significant contribution to a landmark study, uncovering tens of thousands of previously hidden structural variations influencing agriculturally important traits in the mung bean. phys-org.title: NASA space telescope maps magnetic fields of 'Lighthouse' pulsar
phys-org.description: For the first time, scientists have used NASA's IXPE (Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer) to directly measure the magnetic fields of PSR J1101−6101, a pulsar located within what is often referred to as the Lighthouse Nebula. The results provide new insight into the structure of some of the most extreme objects in the cosmos, as NASA continues to explore the secrets of how the universe works. A paper describing the results was published Thursday in The Astrophysical Journal.

phys-org.title: Report finds the justice system in England and Wales is failing to meet people's needs
phys-org.description: The justice system in England and Wales is failing to meet people's needs, with cuts to legal aid forming part of a wider pattern of declining investment and support, warns a new UCL–led report. The findings present a stark picture of a system under strain, with austerity and sustained underfunding having far-reaching consequences.

It's usually found lurking near homes and farms, ports and cities, across Southeast Asia, East Africa, southern Japan and islands across the Indian Ocean. The team calls the dinosaur Uragasaurus kalasinensis and says it is the first formally named mamenchisaurid dinosaur from Thailand.

phys-org.title: New model maps solar storms across 1 million miles around Earth
phys-org.description: A team at the Applied Physics Lab is working to understand the complex science behind predicting invisible threats that can quickly cripple electric grid infrastructure on Earth.

phys-org.title: Virtual tutoring: What started as a pandemic phenomenon has evolved from a temporary fix to an educational fixture
phys-org.description: When Amanda Neitzel first evaluated a live virtual reading-tutoring program called AirReading two years ago, she found what most educators would have predicted: modest results. One semester of live video tutoring nudged struggling early readers forward by roughly a month's worth of learning. But when she ran the study across a full school year, the difference was extraordinary. Literacy gains more than doubled.

phys-org.title: Could exoplanets locked in eternal day and endless night support life?
phys-org.description: Ever so slightly bigger than Earth, the exoplanet LHS 3844b orbits its parent star, LHS 3844, a red dwarf 48.5 light-years from our solar system. Its rotational speed mirrors its orbital speed. The result? One side of LHS 3844b is perpetually bathed in scorching sunlight, locked into a never-ending, blistering hot day, while the other is forever shrouded in darkness so cold that particles are incapable of movement, a state known as absolute zero (zero Kelvin).

phys-org.title: What happened to Australia's snow season? A climate expert explains
phys-org.description: There's nothing like gliding down a snow-covered slope. That is, if you ask the thousands of people who make an annual pilgrimage to our alpine resorts during the Australian winter. But this year, the start to the snow season has been far from spectacular.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: The Israel-Lebanon Recipe for Never-Ending War
proj-syn.description: Lebanon’s political circumstances, together with Iran’s strengthened regional position, make Hezbollah’s complete disarmament highly unlikely. By conditioning Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanon on this outcome—but with no provisions about cutting Hezbollah’s Iranian lifeline—the new framework agreement is dead on arrival.

proj-syn.title: Why This Energy Shock Is Different
proj-syn.description: Unlike recent energy crises, today’s geopolitical shock is destroying supply rather than rerouting it, exposing the limits of the standard policy toolkit. Governments can mitigate its impact on those most exposed, but only if fiscal and monetary policy work in concert.

proj-syn.title: China’s Erasure of Tibet Is Accelerating
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the international community has stood idly by while China has systematically eradicated Tibetan culture and identity. With the authorities stepping up their assimilation efforts, Asia risks not only losing one of its oldest civilizations, but also facing a China that is bigger, bolder, and more powerful than ever.

proj-syn.title: Judging the Enhanced Games
proj-syn.description: If fairness in sports required a level playing field that all who wish to compete could afford, that would be a reason for banning expensive performance-enhancing drugs. But it would be a reason for banning expensive high-tech swimming suits and expensive high-tech running shoes, too.

proj-syn.title: What Is the Digital-Money Debate Really About?
proj-syn.description: Both the US and Europe are moving to create digital money, but neither has the right idea about how to do it. The key is to allow “narrow banks,” which issue money but not credit, to keep their reserves in central banks and provide capped interest payments to coin holders.

proj-syn.title: An Athenian View of American Democracy
proj-syn.description: At 250, America is now producing a mindless, raw power and exponentially growing instability. The possibility of catharsis that characterized the United States at its bicentennial is hard to envisage a half-century later—to the detriment of us all.

proj-syn.title: Low-Cost Solutions to Maternal Mortality Already Exist
proj-syn.description: As foreign aid declines, policymakers in lower-income countries must increasingly focus on making better use of scarce resources. When it comes to maternal mortality, that means investing in simple, proven, and affordable interventions for postpartum hemorrhage, pre-eclampsia, and obstructed labor.

proj-syn.title: Postmodern Economics
proj-syn.description: Eschewing the idea of a single truth, the recently deceased English artist David Hockney showed that the world unfolds before us in ways we cannot fully understand. After long clinging to the pretense of certainty, economists would do well to embrace the same insight.

proj-syn.title: Digital Public Infrastructure Is Now a Strategic Battleground
proj-syn.description: Digital identity platforms, payment systems, and data exchanges promise more efficient, inclusive, and responsive public services. But in an era of geopolitical rivalry and concentrated digital power, those same systems create strategic dependencies that governments can no longer afford to ignore.

proj-syn.title: Should the Bank of Japan Raise Interest Rates?
proj-syn.description: At the beginning of 2013, when "Abenomics" was rolled out in Japan, the yen was significantly overvalued, and looser monetary policy was badly needed. Today, the opposite is true, indicating that interest-rate hikes may well be the right prescription for Japan.

proj-syn.title: How Argentina Can Protect Its Resource Wealth
proj-syn.description: Alaska, Norway, and Chile recognized the economic and political risks that accompany commodity booms and established sovereign wealth funds to preserve their resource revenues. Argentina’s hydrocarbon- and lithium-rich provinces should learn from their experience.

proj-syn.title: Reinventing Development Finance
proj-syn.description: Faced with shrinking concessional finance and rising borrowing costs, Rwanda has worked with the World Bank Group to leverage limited public funds and risk-sharing instruments to unlock private capital at scale and on affordable terms. It's an arrangement holding important lessons for low-income countries that must do more with less.

proj-syn.title: Mamdani’s American Dream
proj-syn.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Independence Day address was a perfect example of ideology in the positive sense of the term. It overturned both the right-wing populist narrative of the United States and the left-wing "woke" critique with a vision that has the potential to mobilize a majority.

proj-syn.title: How Vulnerable Are US Financial Markets?
proj-syn.description: Fueled by more than $1 trillion in borrowed money and rising leverage across the financial system, US stock markets may have entered bubble territory. Two developments could trigger a sharp correction: higher interest rates and a loss of confidence in the handful of tech giants driving the AI boom.

proj-syn.title: Concessional Finance Is Needed More Than Ever
proj-syn.description: As debt burdens rise and climate shocks intensify, sustainable financing mechanisms are becoming indispensable. The Islamic Development Bank’s new concessional fund offers a promising model for mobilizing the resources needed to protect development gains and invest in resilience.

proj-syn.title: Ruling Class Clowns
proj-syn.description: By the end of the 19th-century in the US, it was clear to all interested observers that market power did not automatically or even easily translate into political capital and cultural authority. That is why, unlike the oligarchs of our time, certain Gilded Age capitalists learned how to become a ruling class.

proj-syn.title: The Missing Ingredient for European Tech Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: Europe’s dependence on US technology companies is both an economic challenge and a strategic vulnerability. The European Union’s new Tech Sovereignty Package is a step in the right direction, but without equally ambitious efforts to curb market concentration, it is bound to fall short.

proj-syn.title: In Praise of the World Cup’s Little Guys
proj-syn.description: In a world of great-power rivalry and hyper-scaling tech behemoths, you would be forgiven for thinking that the bulky bully always has the edge. But as this year's World Cup has shown repeatedly, you would be wrong.
